text:
Original [SASRec sampling code](https://github.com/kang205/SASRec/blob/master/sampler.py) rejects every item in the user’s complete training history, drawing uniformly from its complement. For K negatives, independent rejection sampling permits duplicates; retain their multiplicity for a with-replacement objective—deduplication changes the sampling scheme. Seed sampling generators and workers deterministically (training seed 42), keeping draw order reproducible. With the supplied loader returning user=None, exact history exclusion requires sampler-side access to user identity; a truncated sequence cannot reconstruct complete history. Exclusion avoids known-positive negatives, but unseen items can still be false negatives; never inspect held-out labels to filter them.

Distinguish candidate-set cross entropy from a full-softmax approximation. Candidate-set CE uses logits [s_positive/τ, s_negative/τ,…], target index zero, and needs no probability correction. For an importance-estimated partition over the positive plus eligible negatives, use Ẑ=exp(s_positive/τ)+(1/K)Σ exp(s_negative/τ)/q_u(negative), where q_u=1/M_u and M_u is the eligible complement size. Equivalently, subtract log(Kq_u) from negative logits only; the deterministic positive remains uncorrected. This estimates that restricted partition, not the full catalog, and the resulting log loss remains biased. See [candidate-sampling definitions](https://www.tensorflow.org/extras/candidate_sampling.pdf) and [positive-inclusion correction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09331). Lower temperature emphasizes hard negatives; tune on validation because it can amplify false negatives ([analysis](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.02327)). For memory, chunk valid sequence positions before scoring, normalize summed losses by the total valid-position count, and use checkpointing or chunkwise gradient accumulation; merely summing chunk losses can retain every computation graph. PyTorch documents a [chunked linear-CE implementation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.LinearCrossEntropyOptions.html), subject to installed-version availability.
